title: Sort an Array In Place
statement:
Sort an array of integers into ascending order, in place.

## Your function

```
void sort_values(int *values, int count);
```

When it returns, `values[0] .. values[count - 1]` are in ascending order.
There is no return value; the caller's array *is* the answer.

## Watch out

- Write the loops. Calling `qsort` passes the tests and misses the exercise.
- Do not allocate a second array. Insertion sort shifts elements along inside
  the array it was given.
- `count` may be `0`, in which case `values` may be `NULL`, and it may be `1`,
  in which case there is nothing to do.
- Duplicates are ordinary values, not a special case -- but a comparison
  written `>=` instead of `>` will shuffle them about needlessly.

tests.name: empty array
tests.description: count is 0 and values may be NULL. Print nothing and do not dereference the pointer.

tests.name: already sorted
tests.description: The best case: nothing should move.
